scenes.title: Digging the trench
scenes.context: The excavator is digging a 2 m deep trench beside a footpath. A labourer waits to climb in and check the pipe bedding while a tipper truck reverses to collect spoil.
scenes.imageprompt: A realistic photograph of a civil construction site in Australia: an excavator digging a 2 m deep trench beside a footpath, a labourer at the trench edge, a tipper truck reversing nearby, spoil heaped close to the edge.
scenes.teachingnote: Trench collapse cannot be eliminated once the trench is needed; the focus is shoring and safe access.

hazards.name: Trench wall collapse
hazards.anchor: the unsupported trench wall on the left
hazards.why: Soil can collapse without warning and bury a worker in the trench.

eliminate.text: Cannot be eliminated: the trench is needed for the pipe
eliminate.reason: Directional boring is not practicable for this pipe, so the risk must be controlled.

eliminate.text: Ask the labourer to work faster
eliminate.reason: Speed does not remove the hazard; it raises the risk.
Wet soil is more likely to collapse.

reduce.text: Install trench shoring or a trench shield
reduce.reason: Shoring holds the walls so they cannot collapse.

reduce.text: Ladder within 1.5 m of every worker
reduce.reason: A quick way out lowers how badly someone is hurt if a wall moves.

reduce.text: Keep spoil 1 m from the edge
reduce.reason: Spoil near the edge adds load to the wall.

reduce.text: Put up a sign saying Deep trench
reduce.reason: A sign alone does not stop the wall collapsing.

ppe.reason: Protects the head from falling soil and objects.
Noise is not the hazard here.
Sun protection does not protect against a collapse.

hazards.name: Struck by reversing truck
hazards.anchor: the tipper truck reversing on the right
hazards.why: A reversing truck can hit a worker its driver cannot see.

eliminate.text: Set up a drive-through route so trucks never reverse
eliminate.reason: With no reversing, the hazard is removed.
Slower is still reversing near people.
A bigger truck has bigger blind spots.

hazards.name: Fall into the trench
hazards.anchor: the open trench edge by the footpath
hazards.why: A worker or member of the public can fall 2 m into the trench.

eliminate.text: Cannot be eliminated while the trench is open
eliminate.reason: The trench must stay open while the pipe is laid.
Instructions alone do not remove the hazard.

reduce.text: Barrier fencing along the trench edge
reduce.reason: Fencing keeps people away from the edge.

reduce.text: Cover the trench at the end of the day
reduce.reason: An unattended open trench is covered.

ppe.reason: Being seen lowers the chance of being bumped near the edge.
Glasses do not prevent a fall.

distractors.name: Hot work sparks
distractors.why: No welding or cutting is happening in this picture.

distractors.name: Asbestos dust
distractors.why: No old building materials are being disturbed.
